decisions.rationale: Valid observation, low; non-binding, so rejected as a lab defect. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-loop4 on a scratch copy of the frozen export at 60a6b944 (lab.json sha256 0c680786, tests/lab.mjs sha256 9278b451), with npm ci in tests and Node v24.2.0. The shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The reconciler's own solution, written from the README, the starter files and the public tests, passes 26/26 under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT, and its result lines equal expected/solved-summary.txt. Each variant named below is a one-change edit of that solution, run the same way (60 variants plus the solution). Eleven handler variants, those named as run offline below, were also driven against recording stand-ins for httpx and fastapi, not FastAPI TestClient or real httpx. Thirteen shell shapes, those named as run under bash below, ran under bash 3.2.57 with -e and with -eo pipefail, a stub docker that records its stdin per call, and a dummy value; a secrets-context body was run as the value Actions substitutes before the shell starts. The reconciler did not run the loop-2 or loop-3 graders; what earlier graders did is the critics' reproduction. No private overlay, private staging or author work folder was read, and no other critic folder beyond the variant scripts and outputs of the two loop-4 critic folders. Binding rule used throughout this file. A shape binds only when a decision names it, or when an earlier decision's explicit reading of the same list words covers it. Two such readings exist. First, the loop-3 reading that an annotated assignment statement with a value binds its name. Second, the loop-3 reading of the ops-sme-r2-03 words: a cat-opened unquoted heredoc whose body is the secret-mapped variable is h1, unless its content reaches docker login's stdin, which makes it h5. Universal sentences are replaced by the shapes their decisions named. Every other shape is non-binding: it may pass or fail. Message rule (MS): a message printed for a named shape must be true for it. For a non-binding shape, a message is acceptable when it states what the grader requires or did not find and asserts no false property of the learner's code. MS creates obligations only for the shape and message pairs a decision in this file names. Cross-references between items (one item's acceptance requiring another item's list to hold) are cut: each shape binds under the items that name it. Reproduced: a module-level client built with base_url set to API_BASE_URL and the Timeout, bound by a plain assignment written as the body of a one-line if statement, whose get takes the relative path and a dict-literal header, fails tests 24 and 25 and nothing else. Test 24 says "make the call to the shop api with httpx, as the starter does" and test 25 says "no httpx request to the shop api was found: make the call with httpx (directly or through an httpx client), as the starter does". Offline, the handler sends the request with the caller's Authorization value and the Timeout, and raises 401 with no request when no token is sent. Controls: the plain-assignment module client and the annotated one pass 26/26. The SME reports that the loop-3 grader passed this shape. Ruling: the existing words cover it. The loop-2 callee sentence says a name bound to an httpx client "whether by assignment or by a with or async with ... as clause", and the loop-3 reconciliation read c4 as any assignment that binds the name; a one-line if body is such an assignment. This file narrows that reading: for every binding the lists name (a client, a named Timeout, a named headers dict, a URL local), the binding statement is a plain or annotated assignment that begins its own line. Reasons: the list must be finite to converge; the annotated form is the one later form a decision named explicitly (loop 3), while no decision named a compound statement's one-line body; PEP 8 discourages compound statements; and no page, starter or README form uses one. Under the narrowed reading the shape is outside the ops-sme-010 and ops-sme-008 lists. Its two messages meet MS: test 25 states that the grader found no request, and test 24 directs the learner to the starter's form; neither asserts a property of the code. No lab change is required for this finding. A loop-5 change to how the grader reads bindings (see ops-sme-008 and ops-sme-010 in this file) may make this shape pass, but it need not. Process: the operator authorized loop 4 as exactly one bounded loop; no loop 5 is authorized, so any lab byte change needs a fresh operator decision.

Reproduced: (1) the login step's run as cat opening an unquoted heredoc of the secret-mapped variable, sent to the background with a single & and followed on the same line by the README login line; (2) the README login line, then cat opening the same heredoc with its standard output redirected to stderr and piped into docker login --password-stdin. Each passes 26/26. Under bash, with -e and with -eo pipefail, each writes the value to the log once. In (1) docker gets the value from the README pipeline. In (2) the README call gets the value and the second docker call gets empty input. Controls: H1 and the semicolon and && separator shapes fail only test 7, and the cat heredoc piped into docker login with nothing else on the line is not flagged by test 7. Ruling under the loop-3 h1/h5 reading: in both shapes the heredoc is opened by cat, unquoted, with the variable as its body, and its content never reaches docker login's stdin. So h5 does not apply and h1 does. Both shapes are named below as H7 and H8. Heredoc list (closed; it replaces h1-h5 of the loop-2 ops-sme-r2-03 decision and the h1-h3 must-hold of the loop-3 ops-sme-r3-02 decision). V is a variable mapped from secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD in the step's env (for H1 also in the build job's env); R is the README login line (an echo of V piped into docker login with the username variable and --password-stdin); L is docker login with the username variable and --password-stdin. Must fail test 7 with its existing message, which is true for each because bash writes the value to the log (the reconciler's bash runs show this for H1, H2, H3 with a quoted delimiter, both H6 forms, H7 and H8; H3's other spellings print the substituted value the same way and were not run): (H1) an added build-job step whose run block is cat opening an unquoted heredoc whose body is V, with V mapped in that step's env or in the build job's env; (H2) the same with the <<- operator; (H3) cat opening a heredoc, quoted or unquoted delimiter, whose body is the secrets-context expression for REGISTRY_PASSWORD, or the env-context expression of a secret-mapped name; (H6) the login step's run as cat opening H1's heredoc, followed on the opening line by a semicolon and R, and the same with && in place of the semicolon; (H7) the login step's run as cat opening H1's heredoc, followed on the opening line by a single & and R; (H8) the login step's run as R, then a line with cat opening H1's heredoc with its standard output redirected to stderr written as >&2, piped into L. Must not be flagged by test 7: (H4) cat opening a heredoc with a quoted delimiter whose body is only V; (H5) L opening the heredoc itself, with V or the secrets-context expression as the body; (H9) the login step's run as cat opening an unquoted heredoc of V piped into L with nothing else on the opening line, its <<- form, and the same with a command and a semicolon before cat. Test 6 for H5 and H9 is non-binding (the loop-3 ruling on its message stands as optional). Non-binding: every other heredoc shape, including redirect spellings other than >&2 (such as 1>&2, >/dev/stderr or a file), heredocs opened by commands other than cat or docker login, and the non-heredoc echo analogs of H7 and H8. Those analogs may keep passing; if a fix makes them fail test 7, the existing message is true for them, because bash writes the value to the log. Unchanged and not bound here: the pipeline list p1-p3 and q1-q2, the encoder floor and the ::add-mask:: exemption, which bind under ops-sme-r1-07. This finding is met when H7 and H8 fail test 7 with the existing message, and H4, H5 and H9 stay unflagged. Under bash, with -e and with -eo pipefail, the value is written to the log and the second docker call receives empty input. Conflict ruling, against the exact list text. The loop-2 ops-sme-r2-03 list reads "Must fail, for a heredoc opened by cat: (h1) the unquoted heredoc above". Read alone, "the unquoted heredoc above" could mean either the one reproduced step or any heredoc with those properties. The heading ("for a heredoc opened by cat") and the loop-3 reconciliation's explicit reading ("cat with an unquoted heredoc whose body is the secret-mapped variable") settle it as the heredoc's properties. h5 reads "a heredoc fed to docker login --password-stdin, whatever its body". The loop-3 reconciliation placed a cat heredoc in h5 only when its content is fed on to docker login. Here the content goes to stderr and docker receives nothing, so h5 does not apply and h1 does. The education critic appealed to the loop-2 pipeline list, but that list's non-binding sentence names "other middle stages that write to the log by themselves". This redirect is on the opening stage of a heredoc, which the heredoc list governs. So the SME critic's reading holds: the shape is h1 and must fail test 7. It reopens ops-sme-r2-03 under its own list. The SME also counted ops-sme-r1-07 and ops-sme-r3-02, which this shape reached only through cross-references; this file cuts those (see those decisions). It cannot reopen ops-sme-003: this file replaces 003's universal sentence with a closed list that names no heredoc shape, and the shape fails no item of that list. The shape is H8 of the heredoc list in the ops-sme-r4-02 decision of this file. This finding is met when H8 fails test 7 with the existing message, and H4, H5 and H9 stay unflagged. Redirect spellings other than >&2 and the echo analog are non-binding, as that list states. Process: the operator authorized loop 4 as exactly one bounded loop; no loop 5 is authorized, so any lab byte change needs a fresh operator decision.

Three reasons. A text grader cannot decide every shell program that writes to the log. The loop-4 SME recheck reports that the non-heredoc echo analogs of both reopening shapes (an echo of the variable sent to the background before the README line, and an echo redirected to stderr and piped into docker login) pass on both the loop-3 and the loop-4 grader, yet the loop-3 SME recheck recorded 003 resolved. Likewise the loop-2 SME recheck recorded 003 resolved while a cat heredoc printing the secret-mapped variable passed 26/26 (reproduced by ops-reconciler-r2 in its ops-sme-r2-03 decision), and it filed that heredoc separately at low as ops-sme-r2-03. So the sentence was never applied literally. Closed list S, built from the shapes named by the 003 and ops-edu-04 decisions, their loop-1 recheck decisions, and the loop-2 ops-sme-r1-02 and ops-sme-r1-07 lists that elaborated them (S8 and S12-S14 come from those lists). V is a variable mapped from secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD in the step's env unless stated otherwise. Must fail test 7 with its existing message: (S1) the shipped debug step, an echo whose text holds the secrets-context expression; (S2) an added step echoing V, and the same with V mapped in the build job's env and in the workflow's env (the step, job and workflow env named by the replaced sentence); (S3) an added step echoing the env-context expression of V's name; (S4) an echo of V piped into base64; (S5) a printf of V piped into base64; (S6) base64 given V by here-string, with and without a space after the operator; (S7) xxd given V by here-string; (S8) the README login line with a middle tee /dev/stderr stage. Must fail test 6 with the existing message that the login command writes a ${{ ... }} expression into the command text, and must not fail test 7: (S9) an echo of the secrets-context expression piped into docker login --password-stdin; (S10) the same with the env-context expression of the password variable. Must pass tests 6 and 7: (S11) the README form, an echo of V piped into docker login with the username variable and --password-stdin; (S12) printf of V, then tr -d, then that docker login; (S13) the README form wrapped with a backslash continuation, and the README form with a trailing || exit 1; (S14) an ::add-mask:: echo of V on the line before the README form. Non-binding for this item: printenv, env and set -x (as the first reconciliation ruled); every heredoc shape, which binds only under ops-sme-r2-03; every shape that adds a redirect or a background &; and an echo of V redirected to a file. Reproduced on current bytes, each as listed: S1-S8 fail only test 7 with "a run step writes a secret (directly, through an env variable or encoded) to the run log ..."; S9 and S10 fail only test 6 with the ${{ ... }} message; S11-S14 pass 26/26. Under bash, S11 hands docker the value and prints nothing. The two reopening heredoc shapes pass 26/26 and write the value to the log under bash. They bind under ops-sme-r2-03, not this item: see the ops-sme-r4-02 and ops-edu-r4-01 decisions in this file. The echo analogs also pass 26/26 and write the value to the log; they are non-binding everywhere in this file. So the reopen is rejected with evidence, and this item needs no lab change. Note for the gate: T25 closes a high on any reject-with-evidence decision whatever later rechecks say, so a later regression of an S shape shows only as a new finding. Applied to the same words, a Timeout bound by an annotated assignment is that shape. Reproduced: (a1) a module-level httpx Timeout bound by an annotated assignment whose annotation is the httpx Timeout class, passed by that name as the timeout of the httpx.get call, fails test 24 only with "your httpx.Timeout is built but never used: pass it as the timeout argument of the outgoing call (or its client)"; (a2) a local named timeout bound the same way inside the handler and passed by that name fails the same way. Both plain-assignment controls pass 26/26. Offline, each handler passes that Timeout object on the request and raises 401 without a token, so the message is false for a listed shape. The education critic's probe output shows the same failure. No SME recheck tested the shape, and the named-Timeout binding read has no annotation path, so the reconciler infers that the failure predates loop 4, without having run earlier graders. Acceptance (closed; it replaces the loop-2 closing clause for this item). Must pass 26/26: a1; a2; and every loop-2 must-pass shape (the unrelated def with a timeout=None default, a Timeout inline in the call, one bound to a module-level name and passed by it, one bound to a local named timeout and passed by it, one given to the constructor of the httpx client that makes the call in c4 and c5, the page's c6 shape, and c2). Must fail test 24 only, with the built-but-never-used message: (a3) a1's binding with no timeout on the call. Must keep failing test 24 only, with the messages that are true for them: the whole loop-2 must-fail list (the unused module client, the helper with a timeout parameter, the unused lowercase local with no timeout and with a plain number, an unused Timeout under another name, read=None and connect=None, and timeout=None on the call even when its client carries a valid Timeout). Reproduced today as listed: the unused module client and timeout=None on a module client's call. Non-binding: annotations other than the httpx Timeout class, bindings inside a compound statement's one-line body, and a Timeout or client built through a name imported from httpx. T25: 008 stays open until a lab change meets this list and a current SME recheck of 008 resolves it.
